questions.stem: A motor with three pole pairs is operating at 60 Hz. The rotational speed is 1080 rpm. Most nearly, the slip angular velocity is:
questions.explanation: There are 3 pole pairs, so p = 6 poles. Synchronous speed: n_s = 120f/p = (120 × 60)/6 = 1200 rev/min. Fractional slip = (n_s − n)/n_s = (1200 − 1080)/1200 = 0.1. Slip angular velocity = 2π(slip)n_s = (2π rad/rev)(0.1)(1200 rev/min) × (1 min/60 s) = 4π rad/s. The answer is (D).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

questions.stem:
A three-phase synchronous generator produces a 60 Hz waveform when operating at 1200 rpm. How many poles does the generator have?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_138_18.png)
questions.explanation: Use the synchronous speed equation: n_s = 120f/p → p = 120f/n_s = (120 × 60)/1200 = 6 poles. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

questions.stem: A two-pole induction motor operates on a three-phase, 60 Hz line-to-line supply. The motor speed is 3420 rpm, and the rms voltage is 240 V. Most nearly, what is the slip?
questions.explanation: For a 2-pole motor (p = 2), synchronous speed: n_s = 120f/p = (120 × 60)/2 = 3600 rev/min. Slip = (n_s − n)/n_s × 100% = (3600 − 3420)/3600 × 100% = 180/3600 × 100% = 5%. The answer is (A).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

questions.stem:
A DC generator turns at 2000 rpm and has an output of 200 V. The armature constant is 0.5 V·min/Wb, and the field constant of the machine is 0.02 H. Most nearly, what is the field current produced by the generator?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_155_39.png)
questions.explanation: The generated voltage equation is V_a = K_a × n × φ, so φ = V_a / (K_a × n) = 200 V / (0.5 V·min/Wb × 2000 rev/min) = 200 / 1000 = 0.2 Wb. Using φ = K_f × I_f: I_f = φ / K_f = 0.2 Wb / 0.02 H = 10 A. The answer is (B).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

questions.stem:
A 10 hp DC motor draws 42 A. Most nearly, what is the armature voltage?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_148_29.png)
questions.explanation: The mechanical power of a DC motor is P_m = V_a × I_a. Converting hp to watts: P_m = 10 hp × 745.7 W/hp = 7457 W. Solving for armature voltage: V_a = P_m / I_a = 7457 W / 42 A ≈ 177.5 V ≈ 180 V. The answer is (D).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

puzzle_instance.narrative: Fill in the crossword puzzle using the clues related to motors and generators.

words.clue: Machine converting electrical energy to mechanical rotation; speed = n_s × (1 − slip)
Rotating component of an induction machine; its speed relative to synchronous speed defines slip
Stationary winding that creates the rotating magnetic field in an induction motor
Fractional difference between synchronous speed and actual rotor speed
Magnetic p = 120f / n_s; more of these → slower synchronous speed
Rotational force; T = K_a × φ × I_a for DC machines; depends on flux and armature current
